label: TP
reason: User-controlled parameter names flow directly into the HTML response body without sanitization. Attackers can craft requests where the parameter name contains malicious HTML/JavaScript (e.g., ?<script>alert(1)>=BenchmarkTest01417). The code copies this name to "param" (line 63) and writes it to the response (line 66) without HTML encoding, allowing script injection despite the benign-looking logic.

evidence.note: User input retrieved via getParameterNames/getParameterValues loop.
Variable param stores the selected parameter name without validation.
Raw param value written into HTML response body via PrintWriter.format.
